items.abstract:
Change is hard, even when you know the change is worth it. When Wayfair moved to GitHub Enterprise Cloud in 2023, the task of moving 15,000+ repositories and 3,000 active users was daunting. There were numerous security, network, and operational challenges to surmount, but with careful preparation our migration ran smoothly. 

We're releasing the migration toolkit Wayfair developed as open source to make it easier for others to do the same. Join us to learn how we pushed our teams to embrace discomfort and adopt a fail-forward approach, even on our most sensitive code base.

Nobody likes getting a bad report card, and as adults in the workplace, not much has changed since our early school days! So, how do we square human nature—and our enthusiasm to adopt the latest technology—with the need to secure open source software and ensure developers thoroughly understand requirements? 

Join Lelia Bray-Musso, open source architect from Cisco's Open Source Program Office (OSPO), on her journey through introducing Open SFF Scorecard and GitHub Advanced Security solutions to hundreds of GitHub Enterprise Cloud repositories. She'll discuss tactics for deploying tools that maintainers might not realize they need, and the importance of clear communication when enforcing new policy. By the end of this talk, you'll be proud to hang your security report card on the fridge!

He is a 2021 MacArthur Fellow, father of two, and lives in Berkeley, Calif.

items.abstract: Join Chris Colahan, senior security engineer, and Joe Harrington, senior security engineer, as they share Principal Financial Group's journey with application security. Not too long ago, the company relied on multiple source code management systems and a variety of application security tools. They lacked an enterprise inventory of code repositories, a common pipeline solution, and even a shared understanding of application security across the org. This left them with an incomplete picture of risk and a team of unhappy developers, who were often not sure what was expected of them. Chris and Joe will share their story and lessons learned from merging onto a single platform with a common set of developer-focused security tools—all towards the goal of happier developers and better security.

items.abstract:
Tens of thousands of Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) are published each year, and every year the number rises. Yet how many vulnerabilities are actually exploitable and require prioritization? 

Not all CVEs hold equal weight. Some make the news while others fly under the radar. In this discussion facilitated by GitHub's Jon Moroney, security analyst III, and Kevin Backhouse, staff manager of Security Research, you'll take a look at a selection of interesting CVEs, break into groups, and choose one to analyze in more depth. You'll consider and discuss: Is the CVE exploitable? Will it be used for large-scale campaigns or more targeted attacks? We will discuss what’s hype and what’s not and share ideas to improve the process.
